investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps required by the expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource (peer-pod VM slots) reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, meaning all available VM slots on those nodes are already consumed. The other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules, which restrict remote-agent pods to kata/peer-pod capable nodes. Preemption could not help because no lower-priority victims were found on the two eligible nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for 120 s before the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence object and failing all four required-evidence assertions. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] All kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the two eligible nodes are consumed by existing running remote-agent pods or other peer-pod workloads, leaving zero capacity for new pods at the time of the eval run.

[Likely] The node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to kata/peer-pod capable nodes, and only 2 of 6 nodes qualify, amplifying the impact of any capacity shortfall on those nodes.
[Possible] A prior eval run or user-initiated remote agent was not cleaned up and is holding a VM slot, reducing available capacity below the minimum needed for a new probe pod.
[Possible] The cluster has not scaled out to add additional kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, and current demand (from real workloads or concurrent evals) has saturated the fixed pool.

[Lower likelihood] A node that previously provided kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity became NotReady or was cordoned/drained, reducing the eligible node count from a previously larger set to the current 2.

investigation.title: published-observability-snapshot Eval Fail: Stale Snapshot (snapshotAgeMinutes 387 > max 300)
investigation.summary: The eval-only check `published-observability-snapshot` failed because the published status.json at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was 387 minutes old at eval time, exceeding the contract's hard ceiling of 300 minutes (snapshotAgeMinutes max: 300). investigation.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json did not run within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot was 387 minutes old when the eval ran at 2026-07-04T04:09:40Z, meaning the last successful publish occurred approximately 6.45 hours prior. The eval contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482) requires snapshotAgeMinutes <= 300; the observed value of 387 violates that assertion. investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps required by the expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource (peer-pod VM slots) reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, meaning all available VM slots on those nodes are already consumed. The other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules, which restrict remote-agent pods to kata/peer-pod capable nodes. Preemption could not help because no lower-priority victims were found on the two eligible nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for 120 s before the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence object and failing all four required-evidence assertions. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-04T04:04–04:09Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent was never created, and the eval runner could not collect any of the four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state), causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent workload has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation across the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no VM slots remain for new peer-pod scheduling and preemption cannot help. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is scoped to the observability eval environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: published-observability-snapshot Eval Fail: Stale Snapshot (snapshotAgeMinutes 387 > max 300)
investigations.summary: The eval-only check `published-observability-snapshot` failed because the published status.json at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was 387 minutes old at eval time, exceeding the contract's hard ceiling of 300 minutes (snapshotAgeMinutes max: 300). All other public-website sibling checks passed, confirming the public website itself is reachable and this failure is isolated to snapshot freshness, not a broader site outage.
investigations.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json did not run within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot was 387 minutes old when the eval ran at 2026-07-04T04:09:40Z, meaning the last successful publish occurred approximately 6.45 hours prior. The eval contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482) requires snapshotAgeMinutes <= 300; the observed value of 387 violates that assertion. This is an eval-detected staleness condition scoped to the snapshot publishing pipeline, not a user-facing website outage.
proof: failed-check.message: 'snapshotAgeMinutes expected <= 300 but got 387' — the single violated assertion that caused the fail status.

failed-check.evidence: snapshotAgeMinutes=387, maxAgeMinutes=300, source='github-actions', hasLiveSource=true, generatedAtPresent=true — the snapshot exists and was produced by GitHub Actions but is stale.
expected-output.contract: assertion { path: 'snapshotAgeMinutes', max: 300 } defined at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482 — the exact contract boundary that was crossed.

source.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:2168-2170: runner fetches the live payload from args.publishedSnapshotUrl and derives snapshotAgeMinutes from it, confirming the age value reflects the actual published file's timestamp.

sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all passed — the /observability page (HTTP 200, hasAppShell=true) and all 8 marketing routes are reachable, ruling out a site-wide or CDN outage.

source.infra/evals/status/features.json:383: check is registered as required=false, statusImpact='informational', staleAfterMinutes=360 — the registry staleness threshold (360 min) is more lenient than the contract assertion threshold (300 min), a notable discrepancy.
possibleCauses: Most likely — GitHub Actions snapshot-publish workflow missed or skipped one or more scheduled runs, allowing the published status.json to age beyond 300 minutes without a fresh replacement being pushed to GitHub Pages.
Possible — A GitHub Actions runner queue delay, billing pause, or workflow cancellation caused the scheduled publish job to not complete in time, even if it was triggered.

Possible — The snapshot-publish workflow was temporarily disabled, had a failing step that prevented the publish artifact from being written, or the GitHub Pages deployment step failed silently after the workflow ran.

Lower likelihood — A contract/configuration mismatch: the feature registry (infra/evals/status/features.json line 383) sets staleAfterMinutes=360 while the expected-output contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482) enforces max=300; if the workflow runs on a ~360-minute cadence it would routinely breach the 300-minute contract threshold. No evidence of a cadence change is present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges (which is empty), so this is a standing configuration tension rather than a regression.
